rationale: validation_status is fail, with two uncovered_requirements (FR1, SR4) and a dead_check (FR1), plus a mutation_execution_error. Examining the actual mutant content resolves both discrimination gaps as mutant defects rather than evaluator defects. The FR1 mutant (deterministic_fr1_malformed_json) submits a truncated JSON file '{\n' — this SHOULD be detected by any JSON parser and cause a FAIL, yet the mutation_baseline_run/differential show FR1 passing on all mutants including presumably this one; since baseline_run for golden passes and the vulnerable_run also shows FR1 PASS (which is expected, since vulnerable baseline is well-formed JSON), the real issue is the malformed-JSON mutant apparently was not detected — but malformed JSON should trivially fail any real JSON.loads() call, so evaluate.py likely already handles this and the 'dead_check' label stems from the mutant not being run/scored due to the mutation_execution_error (error_runs:1), which is very likely this exact mutant given it's the one exotic domain_specific case most likely to crash the harness's file-diff/copy logic instead of being graded normally. For SR4, the undetected mutant (gate_trojan_detection_cell_substitution_001_SR4_constant_change_001) changes mismatching_inputs from the correct golden values ['0000','0100'] to incorrect values ['1111','1011']. Per SR4's requirement and the golden's own justification, only '0000' and '0100' (i.e., id_auth itself and id_auth with bit 2 flipped) are genuine behavioral discrepancies for this specific fixed id_auth tie-off; '1111' and '1011' may or may not correspond to actual mismatches depending on the concrete id_auth constant encoded in netlist.v, which is not shown to us in the artifact bundle for id_auth's tie-off value. Since the mutant's own expected_detection explicitly claims neither entry corresponds to a real discrepancy, and the check should dynamically simulate and reject fabricated patterns, an undetected outcome here suggests either the mutant coincidentally still simulates true for those inputs (making it non-discriminating / semantically compatible with the golden's dynamic contract) or the harness's mutation run for this specific mutant errored out (matching the reported error_runs:1) rather than actually being exercised and passing. Given both flagged gaps trace to concretely identifiable mutants whose sample values need verification/adjustment (malformed-JSON edge case interacting poorly with the harness's mutation runner, and a mismatching_inputs substitution whose correctness depends on the exact id_auth constant), and the underlying evaluate.py logic for FR1 (JSON validity) and SR4 (dynamic simulation confirmation) both demonstrably work correctly in the differential run (vulnerable_run correctly fails on SR4-related check, golden passes FR1), the appropriate fix is to correct/replace these mutants so they reliably execute and discriminate, not to rewrite the evaluator.
revision_instructions: Two mutants need repair before this case can be retained. (1) The FR1 malformed-JSON mutant (deterministic_fr1_malformed_json, content '{\n') is exactly the kind of edge case that can crash a naive file-copy/diff step in the mutation harness rather than being graded as a normal FR1 failure; investigate whether this mutant is the one causing the reported mutation_execution_error (error_runs:1). If so, keep the mutant's intent (a syntactically invalid submission file) but make sure it is still a well-formed byte sequence that only breaks at the JSON-parsing level (e.g., an unterminated string or a trailing comma) rather than an incomplete brace that might trip up auxiliary tooling; the check itself must simply verify evaluate.py's JSON parse step fails cleanly and reports FR1 FAIL, not crash the outer harness. (2) The SR4 mismatching_inputs mutant currently substitutes the values '1111' and '1011' for the correct discrepancy-triggering values. For this mutant to be a valid, unambiguous negative test, its two id_in values must be verified to NOT produce any grant deviation for the fixed id_auth constant encoded in the netlist -- i.e., simulating the netlist with either of these id_in values against id_auth must agree with a correct XNOR-based reference model. Recompute id_auth's concrete 4-bit value from inputs/netlist.v's tie-off and pick two id_in patterns that are provably behaviorally consistent with a correct comparator (not just plausibly close), so that a dynamic simulation-based SR4 check reliably rejects this submission for lacking a genuine confirmed discrepancy. Regenerate this mutant with those corrected values, or with any input string that is easy to verify offline as producing matching golden/mutant grant behavior, and confirm the mutation harness completes without erroring on it.  Once both mutants are fixed and re-run without execution errors, mutation_score, coverage, and dead_check status should update to reflect genuine discrimination on FR1 and SR4.
